formulas.title: Einstein-Ehrenfest Harmonic Oscillator Adiabatic Invariant
formulas.description: Evaluates the canonical action adiabatic invariant $I$ for a one-dimensional harmonic oscillator of total energy $E$ and slowly varying angular frequency $\omega$, proving that $E/\omega$ stays constant.
formulas.conceptual_definition: For a harmonic oscillator undergoing slow modulation of its stiffness, mass, or pendulum length, the ratio $I = E/\omega$ of instantaneous mechanical energy to angular frequency is an adiabatic invariant.
formulas.intuitive_summary: If you slowly shorten a swinging pendulum so its frequency doubles, the work your hand does lifting the bob automatically doubles the pendulum's energy so that $E/\omega$ never changes.
formulas.interpretation: In phase space, a harmonic oscillator of mass $m$ and frequency $\omega$ traces an ellipse $p^2/(2m) + \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 q^2 = E$ with semi-axes $\sqrt{2mE}$ and $\sqrt{2E/(m\omega^2)}$. Its enclosed area is $\pi \sqrt{2mE} \sqrt{2E/(m\omega^2)} = 2\pi E / \omega$, so dividing by $2\pi$ gives $I = E/\omega$. In quantum mechanics, $E_n = (n + 1/2)\hbar\omega$, meaning classical invariance of $E/\omega$ corresponds directly to the quantum number $n$ remaining fixed during adiabatic evolution.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived directly from the phase-space area invariance of the quadratic harmonic oscillator Hamiltonian under canonical rescalings that preserve the symplectic two-form $dp \wedge dq$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid whenever $|\dot{\omega}|/\omega^2 \ll 1$. If the frequency is modulated near twice the natural frequency ($\omega_{\text{drive}} \approx 2\omega$), parametric resonance breaks adiabatic invariance and pumps energy exponentially into the oscillator.

I.name: Harmonic Oscillator Action Invariant
I.description: Conserved canonical action of the slowly modulated harmonic oscillator.

E.name: Instantaneous Mechanical Energy
E.description: Total kinetic plus potential energy of the oscillator evaluated at the instantaneous parameter value.

\\omega.name: Instantaneous Angular Frequency
\\omega.description: Natural oscillation frequency of the harmonic system varying slowly with time.

formulas.title: Exponential Accuracy of Analytic Adiabatic Invariance
formulas.description: Quantifies the exponentially small net change $|\Delta I|$ in the action variable after an infinitely smooth, analytic parameter ramp with small adiabaticity ratio $\epsilon = T/\tau$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: For an analytic external parameter schedule $\mathbf{R}(\epsilon t)$, the cumulative departure $|\Delta I|$ of the action invariant from its initial value $I_0$ is smaller than any power of $\epsilon$, decaying exponentially as $\exp(-c/\epsilon)$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When a system's parameters are varied smoothly without kinks or jerks, the tiny errors in action conservation cancel out to all polynomial orders, leaving only an exponentially minuscule drift.
formulas.interpretation: In canonical perturbation theory, the formal power series for the exact adiabatic invariant is asymptotic rather than convergent. Optimal truncation at order $N \sim 1/\epsilon$—or equivalently complex-time WKB integration around the nearest turning point or singularity of $\omega(t)$ in the complex time plane—shows that the residual change scales as $|\Delta I| \sim I_0 \exp(-c/\epsilon)$, where $c = 2 \left|\operatorname{Im} \int^{t_*} \omega(s)\,ds\right|$ is determined by the complex singularity $t_*$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from the analytic continuation of phase-space trajectories into complex time and the exponential suppression of high-frequency Fourier components in smooth analytic functions.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Applies strictly as $\epsilon \to 0$ for real-analytic parameter ramps with constant asymptotic limits. If $\mathbf{R}(\epsilon t)$ has a discontinuous $k$-th time derivative, the Fourier tail decays algebraically and $|\Delta I|$ degrades to $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{k+1})$.

\\Delta I.name: Net Action Shift
\\Delta I.description: Cumulative difference between the final and initial action values after a complete adiabatic parameter excursion.

I_0.name: Initial Action Scale
I_0.description: Reference magnitude of the canonical action variable prior to the adiabatic ramp.

c.name: Complex-Time Decay Constant
c.description: Order-unity positive dimensionless constant fixed by the imaginary part of the phase integral to the nearest complex singularity.

\\epsilon.name: Adiabaticity Parameter
\\epsilon.description: Small dimensionless ratio $T/\tau$ comparing the fast orbital period $T$ to the slow external modulation timescale $\tau$.

formulas.title: First Adiabatic Invariant (Orbital Magnetic Moment)
formulas.description: Expresses the first adiabatic invariant $\mu$ of a non-relativistic charged particle of mass $m$ and perpendicular speed $v_\perp$ gyrating in a slowly varying magnetic field of magnitude $B$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The orbital magnetic moment $\mu = m v_\perp^2/(2B)$ is the ratio of perpendicular gyration kinetic energy to local magnetic field strength, remaining conserved whenever $B$ varies slowly over a Larmor radius and cyclotron period.
formulas.intuitive_summary: As a spiralling charged particle enters a stronger magnetic field, it must spin faster around the field line so that its perpendicular kinetic energy grows in exact proportion to the field strength $B$.
formulas.interpretation: Applying $I = \frac{1}{2\pi}\oint \mathbf{P}_\perp \cdot d\mathbf{r}_\perp$ to the circular Larmor orbit of radius $r_L = m v_\perp / (|q| B)$ yields $I = \frac{m}{|q|} \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2B} = (m/|q|)\mu$. Conservation of $\mu$ simultaneously guarantees that the magnetic flux enclosed by a single gyration circle remains constant and produces the magnetic mirror force $F_\parallel = -\mu \nabla_\parallel B$, which reflects particles away from high-field throats.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Emerges from the approximate azimuthal rotational symmetry (gyrophase invariance) of charged-particle dynamics around the local magnetic field direction when spatial gradients satisfy $r_L |\nabla B|/B \ll 1$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Breaks down if magnetic field gradients occur on the scale of the Larmor radius $r_L$, near magnetic null points where $B \to 0$, or under cyclotron-resonant electromagnetic waves. In relativistic plasmas, the invariant generalizes to $\mu = p_\perp^2 / (2 m_0 B)$.

\\mu.name: Orbital Magnetic Moment
\\mu.description: First adiabatic invariant equal to the magnetic dipole moment generated by the particle's cyclotron gyration.

m.name: Particle Mass
m.description: Inertial mass of the gyrating charged particle.

v_\\perp.name: Perpendicular Velocity
v_\\perp.description: Component of the particle's velocity perpendicular to the local magnetic field line.

B.name: Magnetic Field Magnitude
B.description: Strength of the local guiding magnetic field evaluated at the particle's guiding center.

formulas.title: Second Adiabatic Invariant (Longitudinal Bounce Action)
formulas.description: Defines the second adiabatic invariant $J$ as the closed line integral of the guiding-center parallel momentum $p_\parallel$ along a magnetic field line arc length $s$ between conjugate mirror points.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The longitudinal invariant $J = \oint p_\parallel \, ds$ is the phase-space action of a magnetically trapped particle bouncing periodically between two mirror reflection points, conserved during slower azimuthal drift or gradual field evolution.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A particle trapped between two magnetic mirrors bounces back and forth like a ball between slowly moving walls; as long as the magnetic bottle reshapes slowly compared to a bounce period, the longitudinal action $J$ stays fixed.
formulas.interpretation: Using energy conservation $p_\parallel(s) = \sqrt{2m(E - \mu B(s))}$, the bounce integral $J = 2 \int_{s_1}^{s_2} \sqrt{2m(E - \mu B(s))}\,ds$ depends solely on the particle's energy, magnetic moment $\mu$, and the field-line geometry between mirror points $s_1$ and $s_2$. In Earth's magnetosphere, conservation of $J$ restricts drifting Van Allen belt particles to well-defined closed drift shells (Roederer $L^*$-shells), while slow compression of the mirror points accelerates particles via first-order Fermi acceleration.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from the periodic bounce symmetry of guiding-center motion along a closed magnetic flux tube after averaging out the much faster cyclotron gyration.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Conserved provided the magnetic field varies slowly over a bounce period $T_b$ ($T_c \ll T_b \ll T_d$). Pitch-angle scattering by whistler-mode plasma waves or rapid geomagnetic substorms violates $J$ conservation and precipitates particles into the upper atmosphere.

J.name: Longitudinal Bounce Invariant
J.description: Second adiabatic invariant associated with periodic guiding-center oscillation between magnetic mirror points.

p_\\parallel.name: Parallel Momentum
p_\\parallel.description: Component of the particle's linear momentum aligned with the local magnetic field line.

s.name: Field-Line Arc Length
s.description: Spatial distance coordinate measured along the guiding magnetic field line.

formulas.title: Hannay Geometric Angle Surface Integral
formulas.description: Expresses the classical Hannay geometric angle $\Delta \theta_H$ acquired around a closed parameter loop $C = \partial S$ as the negative flux of the Hannay curvature two-form $\mathbf{W}(I, \mathbf{R})$ through any spanning surface $S$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Hannay's formula $\Delta \theta_H = -\iint_S \mathbf{W}(I, \mathbf{R}) \cdot d\mathbf{S}$ isolates the time-reparameterization-invariant geometric angle shift of an integrable Hamiltonian after a slow cyclic excursion of external parameters $\mathbf{R}$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Even after you slowly steer a system's controls around a closed loop back to where they started, the oscillator's angle ends up shifted by a purely geometric amount equal to the curvature flux enclosed by the loop.
formulas.interpretation: In parameter space, the torus-averaged canonical connection one-form $\mathbf{A}_H(I, \mathbf{R}) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \oint_0^{2\pi} p(\theta, I; \mathbf{R}) \nabla_{\mathbf{R}} q(\theta, I; \mathbf{R}) \, d\theta$ is gauge-dependent under angle-origin redefinitions $\theta \to \theta + \chi(\mathbf{R})$. Taking its parameter-space curl defines the gauge-invariant Hannay two-form $\mathbf{W}(I, \mathbf{R}) = \nabla_{\mathbf{R}} \times \left(\frac{\partial \mathbf{A}_H}{\partial I}\right)$ (or in differential-form notation, $d_{\mathbf{R}} \wedge \frac{\partial}{\partial I}\langle p \, d_{\mathbf{R}} q \rangle$), whose surface integral over $S$ determines the observable holonomy $\Delta \theta_H$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises as the $U(1)$ holonomy of the principal torus fiber bundle over parameter space, reflecting the non-integrability of the natural horizontal lift defined by torus averaging.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Vanishes identically for any one-dimensional parameter loop (enclosing zero area) or for time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonians whose canonical coordinates can be chosen real without degeneracy. For the Foucault pendulum on $S^2$, $\mathbf{W}$ is a unit monopole field at the center of the sphere, yielding $\Delta \theta_H = -2\pi \cos\vartheta$ (modulo $2\pi$).

\\Delta \\theta_H.name: Hannay Geometric Angle
\\Delta \\theta_H.description: Extra geometric phase shift in the canonical angle variable beyond the dynamical time integral after one closed parameter cycle.

\\mathbf{W}(I, \\mathbf{R}).name: Hannay Curvature Two-Form
\\mathbf{W}(I, \\mathbf{R}).description: Gauge-invariant curvature vector field in parameter space obtained from the curl of the action derivative of the torus-averaged connection.

I.name: Conserved Action Variable
I.description: Adiabatically invariant action indexing the family of invariant tori.

\\mathbf{R}.name: External Control Parameter Vector
\\mathbf{R}.description: Slowly modulated macroscopic parameters transported around the closed loop $C = \partial S$.

d\\mathbf{S}.name: Parameter-Space Area Element
d\\mathbf{S}.description: Oriented infinitesimal surface area element on the spanning surface $S$ bounded by the parameter cycle $C$.

formulas.title: Semiclassical Hannay-Berry Phase Correspondence
formulas.description: Relates the classical Hannay geometric angle $\Delta \theta_H$ directly to the negative derivative of the quantum Berry geometric phase $\gamma_n(C)$ with respect to the quantum number $n$ in the semiclassical limit.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Berry's semiclassical theorem $\Delta \theta_H = -\partial \gamma_n(C)/\partial n$ proves that the classical angle holonomy of an integrable torus is the exact large-$n$ rate of change of the quantum eigenstate's Berry phase across adjacent energy levels.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A quantum wavepacket is built from neighboring energy eigenstates; the tiny difference in Berry phase between level $n$ and level $n+1$ shifts the classical wavepacket's timing by exactly the Hannay angle.
formulas.interpretation: In the WKB or EBK semiclassical limit where action quantizes as $I_n = (n + \alpha/4)\hbar$ (with Maslov index $\alpha$), a localized wavepacket superposing adjacent eigenstates $|n\rangle$ and $|n+1\rangle$ acquires a relative geometric phase $\gamma_{n+1}(C) - \gamma_n(C) \approx \partial \gamma_n / \partial n$ in addition to its dynamical phase difference $-\int \omega \, dt$. Matching the wavepacket's envelope peak to the classical angle shift $\Delta \theta_H$ yields $\Delta \theta_H = -\partial \gamma_n(C)/\partial n = -\hbar \, \partial \gamma(I, C)/\partial I$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Reflects the semiclassical correspondence between the quantum $U(1)$ Berry connection on projective Hilbert space and the classical canonical connection on the bundle of invariant Lagrange manifolds.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Exact for quadratic Hamiltonians such as the generalized harmonic oscillator at all $n$, and asymptotically exact as $\hbar \to 0$ ($n \to \infty$ at fixed $I = n\hbar$) for general integrable systems away from caustics and degeneracies (diabolical points).

\\Delta \\theta_H.name: Hannay Geometric Angle
\\Delta \\theta_H.description: Classical geometric angle shift accumulated by the action-angle torus around the closed parameter loop $C$.

\\gamma_n(C).name: Quantum Berry Phase
\\gamma_n(C).description: Geometric phase acquired by the $n$-th instantaneous energy eigenstate after adiabatic transport around the parameter loop $C$.

n.name: Principal Quantum Number
n.description: Integer quantum number indexing the quantized invariant torus in the semiclassical EBK spectrum.

formulas.title: Hertzian Granular Contact Force
formulas.description: Gives the nonlinear normal repulsive contact force $F_N$ between two compressed elastic spherical grains as a function of their normal overlap $\delta$, effective Young's modulus $E^*$, and effective radius $R^*$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Hertzian contact mechanics predicts that the normal restoring force $F_N$ between two elastic spheres grows nonlinearly as the three-halves power of their mutual indentation $\delta$, because the circular contact area itself expands with compression.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Squeezing two elastic beads together gets progressively stiffer the harder you push, because flattening the contact patch spreads the load over a wider circle and makes the force rise as $\delta^{3/2}$ rather than linearly like an ideal spring.
formulas.interpretation:
Here $1/E^* = (1 - 
u_1^2)/E_1 + (1 - 
u_2^2)/E_2$ combines the Young's moduli $E_i$ and Poisson ratios $
u_i$ of the two contacting grains, while $1/R^* = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$ is their effective curvature. Because the effective contact stiffness $dF_N/d\delta \propto \delta^{1/2}$ vanishes at zero overlap, acoustic wave speeds in weakly compressed granular packings scale nonlinearly with confining pressure as $c_s \propto P^{1/6}$ rather than remaining constant as in linear elastic solids.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from rotational axisymmetry around the normal contact axis in three-dimensional linear elasticity combined with the geometric parabolic approximation of spherical surfaces near the contact point.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Strictly valid for smooth, non-adhesive, linearly elastic spheres under small strains ($\delta \ll R^*$) below the plastic yield stress. For $\delta \le 0$ (no contact), $F_N = 0$ identically; at high compression, plastic yielding or grain fracture invalidates the elastic $\delta^{3/2}$ scaling.

F_N.name: Normal Contact Force
F_N.description: Magnitude of the repulsive normal force transmitted across the contact patch between two compressed grains.

E^*.name: Effective Contact Modulus
E^*.description: Reduced Young's modulus combining the elastic moduli and Poisson ratios of the two contacting spheres.

R^*.name: Effective Contact Radius
R^*.description: Reduced radius of curvature defined by $1/R^* = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$ for two spheres of radii $R_1$ and $R_2$.

\\delta.name: Normal Overlap Indentation
\\delta.description: Relative normal approach of the two grain centers beyond initial tangential contact.

formulas.title: Janssen's Silo Pressure Saturation Law
formulas.description: Describes the exponential saturation of mean vertical normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(z)$ with depth $z$ inside a cylindrical granular silo of screening length $\lambda$ toward the asymptotic stress $\sigma_{\infty}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Janssen's law models how frictional sidewalls support the weight of a static granular column, causing vertical stress $\sigma_{zz}$ to plateau at $\sigma_{\infty} = \rho_b g \lambda$ over a characteristic depth $\lambda$ instead of growing linearly like hydrostatic fluid pressure.
formulas.intuitive_summary: In a tall grain silo, the walls carry most of the weight through friction, so once you go deeper than a few silo widths, the downward pressure stops increasing and levels off at a fixed ceiling $\sigma_{\infty}$.
formulas.interpretation: Assuming horizontal stress is proportional to vertical stress ($\sigma_{rr} = K \sigma_{zz}$) and wall friction is fully mobilized at $\tau_w = \mu_w \sigma_{rr}$, force balance on a horizontal slice of thickness $dz$ in a cylinder of radius $R$ gives $d\sigma_{zz}/dz + \sigma_{zz}/\lambda = \rho_b g$, where $\lambda = R / (2 \mu_w K)$. Integrating with $\sigma_{zz}(0) = 0$ yields $\sigma_{zz}(z) = \sigma_{\infty}(1 - e^{-z/\lambda})$ with $\sigma_{\infty} = \rho_b g \lambda$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived from axial static force balance under cylindrical symmetry combined with translational invariance along the vertical silo axis away from the top and bottom boundaries.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: In the shallow limit $z \ll \lambda$, expanding the exponential recovers the hydrostatic-like linear profile $\sigma_{zz}(z) \approx \rho_b g z$. In the deep limit $z \gg \lambda$, $\sigma_{zz}(z) \to \sigma_{\infty}$ independently of total fill height, whereas in the frictionless limit $\mu_w \to 0$, $\lambda \to \infty$ and pure hydrostatic scaling is restored.

\\sigma_{zz}(z).name: Mean Vertical Normal Stress
\\sigma_{zz}(z).description: Horizontally averaged downward normal stress inside the granular column at depth $z$ below the free surface.

\\sigma_{\\infty}.name: Asymptotic Saturation Stress
\\sigma_{\\infty}.description: Maximum vertical stress $\rho_b g \lambda$ approached exponentially in the deep-silo limit.

z.name: Depth Below Free Surface
z.description: Vertical coordinate measured downward from the unloaded top surface of the granular column.

\\lambda.name: Janssen Screening Length
\\lambda.description: Characteristic depth scale $R / (2 \mu_w K)$ over which vertical weight is redirected to the confining sidewalls.

formulas.title: Maxwell Isostatic Coordination Criterion
formulas.description: Establishes the minimum average contact coordination number $z_c$ required for mechanical rigidity in a disordered packing of frictionless spheres in $d$ spatial dimensions.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Maxwell's isostaticity criterion $z_c = 2d$ defines the marginal stability threshold where the number of independent repulsive contact forces exactly matches the number of translational degrees of freedom in an assembly of frictionless particles.
formulas.intuitive_summary: For a pile of frictionless balls to lock rigid without wobbly floppy motions, each ball must touch at least twice as many neighbors as there are spatial dimensions—four in 2D and six in 3D.
formulas.interpretation: In $d$ dimensions, $N$ frictionless spheres possess $N d$ translational force-balance equations and $N_c = N z / 2$ unknown scalar normal contact forces (since each contact is shared by two spheres). Equating constraints to degrees of freedom ($N z_c / 2 = N d$) yields $z_c = 2d$. When interparticle friction is present, tangential forces add $d - 1$ unknowns per contact while torque balance adds $d(d-1)/2$ equations per particle, lowering the infinitely rough isostatic threshold to $z_c = d + 1$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from global Euclidean translational invariance in $d$-dimensional space, which fixes $d$ independent force-balance conditions per frictionless particle.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Strictly applies to frictionless spherical particles in the thermodynamic limit ($N \to \infty$) after excluding unstressed rattler grains. For finite systems of $N$ grains under periodic boundaries, $N_c = N d - d + 1$ introduces an $O(1/N)$ correction; non-spherical ellipsoids add rotational degrees of freedom and raise $z_c$ toward $2 d_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

z_c.name: Critical Isostatic Coordination Number
z_c.description: Minimum average number of load-bearing contacts per particle required to eliminate zero-energy floppy modes.

d.name: Spatial Dimension
d.description: Number of Euclidean spatial dimensions (typically $d = 2$ for disks or $d = 3$ for spheres).

formulas.title: Jamming Excess Coordination Scaling Law
formulas.description: Relates the excess average contact number $\Delta z = z - z_c$ above isostaticity to the square root of the excess packing fraction $\phi - \phi_J$ near the jamming transition at Point J.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Above the jamming packing fraction $\phi_J$, the surplus coordination number $\Delta z$ beyond the Maxwell threshold grows with a universal square-root critical exponent $1/2$ independent of the microscopic repulsive contact potential.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Once a jammed sphere packing is squeezed past its critical density $\phi_J$, the number of extra neighbor contacts grows rapidly as the square root of the compression, locking the network stiff.
formulas.interpretation: In three-dimensional frictionless packings, the jamming threshold lies near $\phi_J \approx 0.64$ with $z_c = 6$ and $z_0 \approx 7.8$. The square-root singularity reflects the power-law divergence of the pair correlation function $g(r) \sim (r - d)^{-1/2}$ just outside contact at Point J: compressing the packing by $\phi - \phi_J$ closes near-contact gaps whose cumulative number integrates directly to $(\phi - \phi_J)^{1/2}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Governed by marginal mechanical stability at the zero-temperature, zero-stress Point J critical point, where the pair distribution of near-contacts is constrained by mechanical equilibrium against buckling.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for overcompressed soft repulsive spheres in the regime $0 < \phi - \phi_J \ll 1$ at $T = 0$ and zero shear stress. For $\phi < \phi_J$, the packing unjams and the load-bearing coordination drops discontinuously to zero.

\\Delta z.name: Excess Coordination Number
\\Delta z.description: Average number of contacts per grain in excess of the Maxwell isostatic threshold $z_c$.

z_0.name: Critical Scaling Prefactor
z_0.description: Dimensionless order-unity geometric prefactor depending on spatial dimension and polydispersity.

\\phi.name: Packing Fraction
\\phi.description: Dimensionless fraction of total system volume occupied by the solid grains.

\\phi_J.name: Jamming Packing Fraction
\\phi_J.description: Critical packing fraction at Point J ($\approx 0.64$ in 3D, $\approx 0.84$ in 2D for frictionless spheres).

formulas.title: Jamming Shear-to-Bulk Modulus Scaling
formulas.description: Expresses the linear vanishing of the ratio of shear modulus $G$ to bulk modulus $B$ with excess coordination $\Delta z$ as a jammed solid approaches the isostatic Point J.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Near the jamming transition, a disordered sphere packing resists isotropic compression far more strongly than shear deformation, causing the elastic ratio $G/B$ to vanish proportionally to the excess contact number $\Delta z$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Right at the edge of jamming, a disordered pile of spheres is easy to shear sideways even though it still resists being squeezed uniformly, so its shear-to-bulk stiffness ratio shrinks smoothly to zero with $\Delta z$.
formulas.interpretation: For harmonic repulsive spheres, the bulk modulus $B$ jumps discontinuously to a finite constant at $\phi_J$ while non-affine grain relaxations suppress the shear modulus to $G \propto \Delta z \propto (\phi - \phi_J)^{1/2}$. For Hertzian spheres ($F_N \propto \delta^{3/2}$), both moduli acquire an extra $(\phi - \phi_J)^{1/2}$ stiffness factor ($B \propto (\phi - \phi_J)^{1/2}$, $G \propto (\phi - \phi_J)$), yet their dimensionless ratio $G/B = c_0 \Delta z$ remains universally proportional to $\Delta z$ across all repulsive contact laws.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Reflects the breakdown of affine continuum elasticity near marginal isostaticity, where soft non-affine displacement fields relax shear energy without violating isotropic volume constraints.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: As $\Delta z \to 0^+$ at Point J, $G/B \to 0$ and the Poisson ratio approaches the incompressible fluid limit $\nu \to 1/2$ in 3D (or $1$ in 2D). Far above jamming ($\Delta z \sim O(1)$), non-affine fluctuations subside and $G/B$ approaches standard crystalline solid values.

G.name: Static Shear Modulus
G.description: Linear elastic modulus measuring resistance of the jammed packing to volume-preserving shear strain.

B.name: Static Bulk Modulus
B.description: Linear elastic modulus measuring resistance of the jammed packing to isotropic uniform compression.

c_0.name: Dimensionless Elasticity Prefactor
c_0.description: Order-unity geometric coefficient linking excess coordination to the shear-to-bulk modulus ratio.

\\Delta z.name: Excess Coordination Number
\\Delta z.description: Average number of contacts per grain above the Maxwell isostatic threshold $z_c$.

formulas.title: Granular Inertial Number
formulas.description: Defines the dimensionless inertial number $I$ governing dense granular flows as the ratio of the microscopic grain rearrangement time $d / \sqrt{P / \rho_p}$ to the macroscopic shear timescale $1 / \dot{\gamma}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The inertial number $I$ is the single dimensionless control parameter of local dense granular rheology, quantifying whether a sheared granular assembly behaves quasistatically, as a dense frictional liquid, or as a rapid collisional gas.
formulas.intuitive_summary: The inertial number $I$ compares how fast you shear a granular flow against how quickly a grain can snap into a nearby hole under the confining pressure $P$.
formulas.interpretation: Dimensional analysis of dry rigid grains of diameter $d$ and intrinsic density $\rho_p$ sheared at strain rate $\dot{\gamma}$ under confining pressure $P$ yields $I$ as the unique dimensionless group. Within the $\mu(I)$ constitutive framework, both the effective friction coefficient $\mu(I) = \mu_s + (\mu_2 - \mu_s)/(I_0/I + 1)$ and the dilatant packing fraction $\phi(I) = \phi_c - a I$ are single-valued functions of $I$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Emerges from Buckingham Pi dimensional invariance for athermal, rigid, dry granular assemblies lacking an intrinsic microscopic viscosity or thermal velocity scale.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: For $I \ll 10^{-3}$, the flow is quasistatic and rate-independent with enduring force chains ($\mu \to \mu_s$). For $10^{-3} \lesssim I \lesssim 10^{-1}$, dense liquid-like $\mu(I)$ flow prevails; for $I \gtrsim 10^{-1}$, binary collisions dominate and kinetic granular gas theory applies. When interstitial fluid viscosity $\eta_f$ dominates inertia, $I$ is replaced by the viscous number $J = \eta_f \dot{\gamma} / P$.

I.name: Inertial Number
I.description: Dimensionless ratio of microscopic inertial rearrangement time to macroscopic shear deformation time.

\\dot{\\gamma}.name: Shear Strain Rate
\\dot{\\gamma}.description: Macroscopic velocity gradient driving continuous plastic deformation of the granular medium.

d.name: Mean Grain Diameter
d.description: Characteristic linear size of the individual solid particles comprising the granular assembly.

P.name: Confining Normal Pressure
P.description: Local isotropic or normal confining stress pressing the sheared granular layers together.

\\rho_p.name: Intrinsic Grain Material Density
\\rho_p.description: Solid mass density of the individual grain material (distinct from bulk packing density $\rho_b = \phi \rho_p$).

formulas.title: Beverloo's Hopper Discharge Law
formulas.description: Predicts the steady mass discharge rate $W$ of dry granular material flowing under gravity $g$ out of a circular silo orifice of diameter $D$ in terms of bulk density $\rho_b$, grain diameter $d$, and empirical constants $C$ and $k$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Beverloo's law expresses the fill-height-independent mass flow rate of grains exiting a hopper, scaling as the $5/2$ power of the effective orifice diameter $D - k d$ because Janssen screening decouples exit speed from silo depth.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Unlike water draining faster from a full tank than a nearly empty one, sand pours from a hopper at a constant rate determined only by gravity and the opening width minus a narrow dead zone around the rim.
formulas.interpretation: Because Janssen sidewall friction screens the overburden pressure, grains accelerate from rest across a free-fall arch of height proportional to the effective orifice width $D_{\mathrm{eff}} = D - k d$, reaching exit velocity $v \propto \sqrt{g D_{\mathrm{eff}}}$. Multiplying bulk density $\rho_b$ by exit area $\propto D_{\mathrm{eff}}^2$ and velocity $\propto \sqrt{g D_{\mathrm{eff}}}$ yields $W \propto \rho_b \sqrt{g} (D - k d)^{5/2}$, with $C \approx 0.58$ and $k \approx 1.4$ for smooth spherical particles.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from dimensional analysis of gravity-driven granular flow once Janssen screening eliminates the total column height $H$ as a relevant length scale.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for dry, coarse, cohesionless grains ($d \gtrsim 500\,\mu\text{m}$) in silos whose fill height exceeds roughly $2 D$ and whose orifice satisfies $D \gtrsim 6 d$. When $D \lesssim 5 d$, permanent force-chain arches intermittently clog the aperture; for fine powders, interstitial air drag reduces $W$ below the Beverloo prediction.

W.name: Mass Discharge Rate
W.description: Steady mass of granular material exiting the hopper orifice per unit time.

C.name: Beverloo Discharge Coefficient
C.description: Dimensionless empirical discharge constant (typically $0.55$ to $0.65$ depending on grain friction).

\\rho_b.name: Bulk Granular Density
\\rho_b.description: Macroscopic mass per unit total volume of the flowing granular packing ($\rho_b = \phi \rho_p$).

g.name: Gravitational Acceleration
g.description: Local acceleration due to gravity driving downward discharge through the hopper opening.

D.name: Orifice Diameter
D.description: Physical diameter of the circular discharge opening at the base of the silo or hopper.

k.name: Empty-Annulus Shape Factor
